root_idea.summary: The root denotes bringing two or more things into conjunction, mutual fit, or close association.
root_idea.development: From joining things together, the lexicon develops senses of gathering groups, drawing something toward another thing or oneself, compacting or enclosing, reciprocal closeness, and figurative appropriation.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic imperative is presented under the normalized Form I perfect citation headword ضَمَّ.

senses.definition: To draw or bring one thing close to another; to join or gather them together.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic imperative, the construction with إِلَى expresses drawing the hand toward the wing or drawing the wing toward oneself, that is, bringing the bodily parts close together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gather or collect things or people into a group, and to join one thing to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of people collecting themselves or becoming gathered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To embrace or press someone to the bosom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily application of drawing one person close to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compact, compress, or contract something by drawing its parts together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the drawing together of parts or extremities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compose or reorganize what is scattered or disordered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use, especially of affairs or circumstances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be gentle, courteous, accommodating, or easy to deal with.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative expression involving contracting one's side or wing from people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To comprise or enclose something, or to grasp it; with property, to take all or part of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be something enclosed or grasped, or property taken to oneself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near to, become close to, or become conjoined with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III may also describe remaining conjoined with someone while engaged in one affair, or a thing becoming adjoined to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a person or thing accompanied by another, or to append one thing to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes making a written item accompany or comprise another item.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or devour something altogether.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action is directed toward consuming or taking the whole of the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near to one another or become mutually conjoined.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction describing members becoming close together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw oneself together physically.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of compacting the body in prostration or sitting during prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become drawn, brought, or gathered together; to become contracted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a thing or group becoming collected or drawn together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To join oneself to, attach oneself to, or resort to someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction with إِلَى can express betaking oneself or repairing to the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fold around, infold, or enclose something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction with عَلَى describes something becoming drawn together upon or around the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw, bring, or gather something to oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VIII uses ط in place of ت because of the preceding ض.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw close together, or to press and crowd upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may be reciprocal or may describe people pressing together upon an object or person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To comprise or enclose something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an enclosing structure, such as ribs enclosing what is within them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or appropriate all the property, drawing it to oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reduplicated Form I expression emphasizing comprehensive taking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To encourage one's ardor or become courageous in heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a lion, to roar or utter a cry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated verbal noun is ضَمْضَمَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An embrace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of instance or occurrence derived from the embracing sense of ضَمَّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A group of horses assembled from different quarters for a race.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collection is named for the horses being assembled together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing, thread, string, cord, or similar object used to draw one thing to and join it to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The item functions as a means of attachment or conjunction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A valley running between two long hills, or a valley with water flowing between them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact nuance differs in the transmitted explanations, but the term denotes the intervening valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An adjunct or associate attached to another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of one person made the companion or adjunct of another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One of the two sides or boards that hold and enclose a book, saddle, or camel saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually used in the dual in expressions for the paired enclosing sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who collects seed-produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational or agent noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A musterer or gatherer of a people or group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized feminine form used for the person who assembles a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A want or object of want that brings a person to have recourse to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic nominal use describing what draws someone toward a resource or course of action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion that grasps everything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description emphasizes the lion's seizing or taking hold of whatever it encounters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Angry, bold, or daring; also an angry lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The human application is to a man; the animal application is to a lion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Extremely niggardly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who takes or gets everything within his grasp, drawing it to himself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive agent noun describing comprehensive appropriation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who eats excessively, appropriates food to himself, or eats without becoming satiated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may emphasize either inordinate appetite or exclusive appropriation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A niggardly man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive human use distinct from the appetite-related use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bundle or joined collection, especially of books or writings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural أَضَامِيمُ is used for such bundles or collections.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or collection of people, horses, or the like brought together from different groups.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The people are mixed rather than belonging to one stock; the same idea is applied to collections of horses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stones or collections of stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural use recorded for the term in contexts involving grouped stones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where military forces assemble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun referring to the gathering of troops.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean or slender, including lean and lank in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative descriptive use explained as if one part were drawn and joined to another.
